source_text: Nam Manichaeos deseris in vituperatione suum et caprarum, quos in humanae naturae criminatione comitaris; cum quibus etiam in Christo non speciem carnis, sed rationem evertis exempli. Submoves etiam a Christo verbis interim naturale peccatum, ne et ipsum sub potestate diaboli collocare videaris, quod non fecit vel ipse Manichaeus. Sed laudas Hieronymum, qui ita eum non metuit blasphemare, ut dicat illum familiaritatem cum voluntariis quoque iniisse criminibus. Ita inter diversas amicorum sordes et commenta volutatus sine deflexu, in Catholicorum solum efferaris iniurias, quia dicunt Deum mali auctorem non esse, homines qui ab eo fiunt, malos non esse naturaliter, leges Dei iustas esse, imaginem eius posse declinare a malo et facere bonum; Christum nec in membris, nec in praeceptis, nec in iudiciis ullum perpetrasse peccatum. Atque ideo si tu assertione veritatis aegrescas, credimus tamen prudentes instrui, nonnullosque etiam de his quos mendacia tua sauciarunt, posse sanari.
pass_a_gloss: For you desert the Manichaeans in the blaming of swine and of goats, whom you accompany in the accusation of human nature; with whom also in Christ you overturn not the appearance of flesh but the reason of the example. You also remove from Christ by words meanwhile natural sin, lest you seem to place even him under the power of the devil, which not even Manichaeus himself did. But you praise Jerome, who so did not fear to blaspheme him that he says he entered familiarity even with voluntary charges. Thus rolled without deflection among the diverse filths and inventions of friends, you are carried only into injuries of the Catholics, because they say God is not the author of evil, humans who are made by him are not evil naturally, the laws of God are just, his image can decline from evil and do good; Christ perpetrated no sin either in members, or in precepts, or in judgments. And therefore if you grow sick at the assertion of truth, we nevertheless believe that the prudent are instructed, and that some even of those whom your lies have wounded can be healed.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: For you abandon the Manichaeans when they disparage pigs and goats, though you accompany them in accusing human nature. With them, too, you overthrow in Christ not the appearance of flesh but the basis of his example. At least in words, you also remove natural sin from Christ, lest you seem to place him too under the devil’s power, something not even Manichaeus himself did. Yet you praise Jerome, who does not fear to blaspheme him by saying that he entered into familiarity even with voluntary crimes. So you roll without turning aside among your friends’ various filth and inventions, and rage in abuse only against the catholics. For they say that God is not the author of evil; that human beings made by him are not naturally evil; that God’s laws are just; that his image can turn away from evil and do good (compare Genesis 1:26–27; Psalm 34:14); and that Christ committed no sin in his members, his commands, or his judgments (compare 1 Peter 2:22). Therefore, although the assertion of truth makes you sick, I believe that thoughtful people are instructed, and even some of those wounded by your lies can be healed (Genesis 1:26–27) (Psalm 34:14) (1 Peter 2:22).
